To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present an end- to- end approach for the synthesis of reactive mission plans and code for an Atlas humanoid, including reaction to failures of low-level tasks.
we have developed a method for the automatic generation and implementation of high-level robot behaviors that can be guaranteed to satisfy their specifications in the presence of low-level failures.

(1) the proposed approach enables non-expert users to specify a task for a robot in a high-level language and automatically synthesize a reactive, verifiably correct, mission plan; (2) the approach is applicable to real-world, robotic systems with complex dynamics and high-level tasks that include the reaction to possible low-level failures; and (3) we demonstrate the approach using Team ViGR's software and Atlas, a 1.8m tall humanoid robot.
In summary, our research is concerned with
enabling the automatic generation of high-level robot behaviors, including reaction to failures, from high-level descriptions of tasks.
the development of formal methods for the automatic generation and implementation of high-level, reactive behaviors for complex robotic systems.
the automatic synthesis of reactive mission plans that can be executed in real-world systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper proposes a novel end-to-end methodology for generating code for reactive behaviors of a complex robot system that is formally verified.

the work in this thesis has successfully demonstrated the applicability of formal verification techniques to the design and implementation of high-level robot behaviors, thus bridging the gap that exists between the theory of synthesis and its application in real-world, complex robotics systems.
we have successfully demonstrated the application of formal techniques for reactive synthesis to complex robotic systems, and have shown that the approach can be applied to a real-world robot.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the formal synthesis approach is a promising direction for the future of robot programming.
we have successfully applied the theory of formal methods to the real-world problem of reactive behavior synthesis for an autonomous robot.
we have demonstrated the application of formal verification and synthesis techniques to complex systems such as a humanoid robot.
The main takeaway from our work is that
formal synthesis techniques are applicable to real-world, robotic systems, even those that are complex, and that they are capable of automatically producing correct, reactive, high-level behaviors.
the synthesis of complex robotic behaviors is now within reach of non-expert users.

formal synthesis can be applied to real-world robotic systems and is a promising approach to enable non-expert users to specify high-level robot behaviors and guarantee that they achieve the desired task or correctly react to low-level failures.
